Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:40: As for what is said (Proverbs 28:14) "happy is the man who fears always," our Sages, of blessed memory, explain that this refers to words of Torah (Berachot 60a): they said, a certain student was walking behind Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosi, and saw that he was fearful [while studying]. He said to him, "you are sinning, for it is written (Isaiah 33:14) 'the sinners in Zion are afraid.'" He said to him, "but is it not written, 'happy is the man who fears always'?" "That," he said, "is written concerning words of Torah" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:41: Likewise, one must fear in every place that has holiness, such as a synagogue and the like, as our father Jacob, peace be upon him, said when he saw the vision of the ladder (Genesis 28:17) "how awesome is this place; this is none other than the house of God" - meaning, it would not have been fitting for me to sleep here. So too David the king, peace be upon him, said (II Samuel 6:9) "and David feared the Lord that day, and said, how shall the Ark of the Lord come to me?" - thinking that he was not worthy, because of his deeds, of the Ark's holiness, and perhaps he would not treat it with the honor due to it and would blemish its glory. Along these lines David said (Psalms 5:8) "I will bow toward Your holy Temple in fear of You" - this is [the meaning of] "you shall fear My sanctuary" (see Leviticus 19:30).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:42: So too Rashbi, of blessed memory, explains (Zohar, portion of Yitro, 79b): it is taught, Rabbi Yosi said, one day I was standing before Rabbi Yehudah the Elder and asked him about what is written (Genesis 28:17) "and he was afraid, and said, how awesome" - what did he see that made him say it was awesome? He said to me, he saw the completeness of holy faith found in that place, in the manner of what is above, and wherever completeness is found, it is called "awesome." I said to him, if so, why do they translate it as "fear" and not "complete"? He said to me, there is no fear except in a place where completeness is found, and wherever completeness is found, it is called "awesome," as it is written (Psalms 34:10) "fear the Lord, His holy ones, for there is no lack for those who fear Him" - implying that it says "for there is no lack," and where there is no lack, completeness is found - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:43: According to his view, the explanation of the verse "fear the Lord, His holy ones" is that the Name YHVH is complete, and you must fear it; and the proof of this is that His fearers are complete and lack nothing, since fearing the Name brings them completeness - if so, it appears certain that the Name YHVH is the source of completeness, and one must fear it; and from this we infer, for any place the Shechinah rests, which is the totality of the ten [sefirot] comprised within YHVH, that completeness is there, and one must fear it. This is the plain sense of the passage.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:44: When we broaden the matter further, we say that the place of completeness is the Holy One, blessed be He, together with His Shechinah, for both together are a complete "Adam" - for a male without a female is half a body, and is deficient; therefore, in every place where there is completeness, which is union, fear rests, since it is known that the place of fear is the Shechinah. And the root of essential fear is to be over all the upper beings, since He is great and rules, etc., as I explained, and He rests only upon a complete place and a properly arranged throne, as is known, and the essence of completeness is union. Therefore it says, "he saw the completeness of holy faith," which is the reality of the union of all of Atzilut with the Emanator, and therefore fear rests there - this is [the meaning of] "fear the Lord" - the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:45: He mentions fear in respect of the Name YHVH, since in this Name the Cause of causes is unified, and therefore those who cleave to this Name and fear Him lack nothing, since this Name is praised above all names and indicates the complete union, and in it rests the Cause of causes, as is explained in the Gate of Fear, chapter 1, in the passage we quoted from the words of Rashbi from the Tikkunim. And for this reason the verse states it in a negative form, "for there is no lack," because the matter depends on that which is highest, highest, in a place where there is no lack of flow at all.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:46: Among the merits of fear is what is said in the Tikkunim (5b), on the verse "fear the Lord, His holy ones, for there is no lack for those who fear Him" - it says, there shall be no lack in his study, and no lack in his soul, and no lack in his good deeds, for there is no lack and poverty like the lack of Torah and its commandments, as the masters of the Mishnah established, "there is no poverty except of Torah and the commandments" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:47: Further, concerning the merit of fear, it says in the midrash, on the verse (Proverbs 31:30) "grace is false and beauty is vain," etc. - his words: "another interpretation: 'grace is false' - neither beauty nor wealth is accepted before the Holy One, blessed be He; what does He seek? Fear of sin, as it is said, 'a woman who fears the Lord, she shall be praised.' How much did our father Abraham, peace be upon him, do before the Holy One, blessed be He, and yet he was not praised for it - for what was he praised? That he feared sin, as it is said (Genesis 22:12) 'now I know that you fear God'" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:48: Incidentally, let us understand what "fear of sin" has to do with the phrase "fear of God," and what "fear of sin" itself means. The matter is understood by what our Sages, of blessed memory, say in Bereishit Rabbah concerning the Binding of Isaac - their words (56:7): "'and He said, do not lay your hand upon the lad' - and where was the knife? Three tears fell from the ministering angels upon it and ruined the knife. He said to Him, then what shall I do to him - I will strangle him. He said to him, 'do not lay your hand upon the lad.' He said to him, I will draw a drop of blood from him. He said to him, 'do not do anything [me'umah] to him' - not even a blemish [mumah]" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:49: The matter is that in all these alternatives our father Abraham, peace be upon him, needed to say "I will strangle him," "I will draw blood from him" - why did he need this, once the knife was ruined? Rather, he feared sin, [thinking] perhaps I have some small sin that I have not been careful about, such that my offering will not be accepted, since the knife was ruined. Along these lines of fear, Sefer HaRokeach writes - his words: "the root of fear is that it is hard for him to act, yet he abandons his desire and his inclination for the fear of the Lord, and fears lest he not be perfect before the Lord, like Abraham, of whom it is said, 'for you fear God,' since this is greater than the [other] trials" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:50: "Fear of sin" applies even to a small sin, and therefore in Ra'aya Meheimna "fear of sin" is explained in Binah, as we quoted above at the end of chapter 3. The matter is that the higher a person rises, the more he is scrutinized, along the lines of (Psalms 50:3) "and it is very tempestuous round about Him." Its explanation is like the parable of servants who serve the king: the king has many servants - some stand before him in the innermost chamber where the king himself is, and others serve in the outer chamber, and others in his courtyard, and others in his city, and others outside his city, and all serve and all fear the king, but the closer one is, the more he fears, and the further one is, the more the fear diminishes; and those who are truly before him stand in awe and fear lest any fault be found in them at all. Therefore it says, "and it is very tempestuous round about Him" - those who are truly round about the King are tempested very much; wherever it says "very" it is without measure, as is explained in the Zohar, portion of Vaera (27a).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:51: So too, when the righteous man thinks that he always stands before His providence, blessed be He, and that through the Cause of all causes and the Reason of all reasons, whose providence never ceases for a single moment from any created being, he finds himself round about the King, in the sense that the King has drawn him near to stand before Him, having made known to him the secrets of His Palace - and this is certainly on account of the supernal soul given to the righteous man more than to the rest of the common people - he must fear lest the supreme King find any fault in him, causing the light of His providence and His flow to be withheld from his soul, and He distance Himself from him, whereupon his soul is found blemished.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:52: Proof of this is what Rashbi says (portion of Vayakhel 217b) - his words: "Rashbi said to his colleagues, and you, colleagues, behold the Holy One, blessed be He, now delights in those words that are being crowned in that way, and you stand before your Master in your holy images - for I, at the time I see you and gaze at your images, see in you that you are marked with the secret of Adam, and I know that your image is prepared above; and thus the righteous are readied to be recognized in the eyes of all and to show a holy countenance before the whole world - this is [the meaning of] (Isaiah 61:9) 'all who see them shall recognize them, that they are a seed the Lord has blessed.'" Meanwhile he saw Rabbi Yosi thinking about worldly matters. He said to him, "Yosi, arise, complete your image, for you are missing one [i.e., something]" - Rabbi Yosi arose and rejoiced in words of Torah and stood with him. Rashbi gazed at him and said to him, "Rabbi Yosi, now you are complete before the Ancient of Days, and your image is complete" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:53: This is the aspect of supernal fear: that it should be in his eyes as though he always stands before the Cause of causes, for his image is engraved above in the secret of the soul, as we elaborated above in chapter 9; and if, God forbid, he blemishes even with a mere thought, his soul is found blemished and distanced from the light of the face of the supreme King, as is explained in the passage I brought. Let a person consider how much awe he would feel if he stood before Rashbi, peace be upon him, who recognized in a person's face even a mere thought, as is explained - just as his colleagues stood in awe before him, for while standing before him, they stood truly before the Shechinah - in this same respect a person must fear the Creator standing before him and recognizing his thoughts, as is known, and this is the matter of "and it is very tempestuous round about Him," which I explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:54: According to how a person cleaves to his Creator and fears Him, so is the Creator found with him, along the lines of "if you seek Him, He will be found by you" (I Chronicles 28:9); and just as we find He was found with the ancients, whose prayer was heard immediately and whose speech made an impression above, as is said in the Zohar, portion of Vayechi (218a), concerning the story of Rabbi Yitzchak - "the Throne of his Master drew near to the wings of Rabbi Shimon" - and likewise the story of Choni HaMe'agel and many like him found in the Talmud (Ta'anit, chapter 3).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:55: There is a sin that blemishes the ruach but does not blemish the nefesh, for according to the ascent of the ruach, so are they exacting; and likewise there is a matter that blemishes the neshamah but not the ruach, such as being precise about some mitzvah not properly attended to. The reason is that according to the fineness of the neshamah, so a very light matter blemishes it - and this is called "fear of sin," and this is called "fear of God," who is the supreme God in Binah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:56: Proof of this: it says there in Midrash Rabbah, after the passage we quoted above (Genesis 22:12) "for now I know that you fear God" - "now I know" for all, that you love Me. So too in Tractate Sotah (chapter 5, mishnah 5), they explain that "fear of God" said of Abraham is out of love. And our Sages, of blessed memory, were compelled to say it was out of love because performing a mitzvah in darkness and with alacrity indicates love, and this we find with our father Abraham, peace be upon him (Genesis 22:3) "and Abraham rose early in the morning," etc., "and saddled his donkey and took with him," etc. - here they compared this level of fear to actual love; and it is known that love is above, and although love is also found below, in the Shechinah, which is a lesser love, its essence is above.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:57: It is already possible to say that these are differing midrashim: the passage from Proverbs, which expounds "fear of God" as fear of sin, holds that this is below, in the Shechinah, in whom fear of sin also applies; while Midrash Rabbah holds that "fear of God" is above, in the place of love, as explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:58: It may also be said that the Shechinah is called "a woman who fears the Lord" from the side of Binah, along the lines of what is explained in the Tikkunim (6a), that the Shechinah is called "fear" from the side of Gevurah - and now "fear of sin" is fitting above, as Ra'aya Meheimna explains, and there is [the level of] "God" [Elohim], and from there fear flows downward.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:59: Further, we may say concerning "fear of sin" that "chet" [sin] denotes deficiency, as in (I Kings 1:21) "and I and my son Solomon will be [chata'im] deficient/reckoned as sinners"; and the fear is that he fears lest the flow be diminished because of him, whether above, from the supernal Mother, that she be removed from over the children, or from the lower Mother, that the flow be diminished from the six directions, that they not bestow upon her, along the lines of what she says, "my mother's sons were angry with me" (Song of Songs 1:6), as is explained in the Zohar (see Tazria 45b; Acharei 59b).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:60: Further, we may say concerning "fear of sin" that not only in sin but even in a good deed fear applies, for he fears lest he has not repaired it or done all that is needed, according to the obligation of service to God, blessed be He, for His great kindnesses toward His creatures, as the pious author of Chovot HaLevavot elaborates (Gate of the Service of God, chapter 3); and this too is "chet," along the lines mentioned, denoting deficiency - meaning, perhaps he is lacking in the obligation of service incumbent upon him as it should be, for anyone whom the Holy One, blessed be He, favors with wisdom or wealth or for whom He performs miracles is obligated to greater and greater service, so as not to be ungrateful for the Creator's abundant goodness toward him. This is learned from what the Holy One, blessed be He, rebuked Eli concerning his sons (I Samuel 2:27) "did I not reveal Myself to your father's house when they were in Egypt... and did I not choose it out of all the tribes of Israel," etc.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:1: Having spoken of the matter of fear and its aspects, as we have found in the words of Rashbi and the words of our Sages, of blessed memory, we said that we would speak in this chapter of several particular things a God-fearing person should do, so that his fear be recognized in him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:2: In general, one must be careful in all matters that involve the honor of the Lord, and connect honor with fear, because we find two aspects concerning fear: one, fear from the side of negative commandments, as is said in the Tikkunim (146b), "her fear is in the negative commandments," and fear unqualified is not to transgress the commandment of the King. And there is fear to fulfill positive commandments, as it is written (Psalms 128:1) "happy is everyone who fears the Lord, who walks in His ways," and it says (ibid. 112:1) "happy is the man who fears the Lord, who delights greatly in His commandments" - for if He commanded that one perform His mitzvah, and he neglects and refrains from fulfilling the King's command, he is punished, and this is certainly a matter of reason. So too our Sages, of blessed memory, say (Menachot 41a) that at a time of wrath they punish for [neglecting] a positive commandment.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:3: Likewise, the way of honor, that we are obligated to honor our Maker, has these two aspects mentioned: one, to honor Him out of fear of Him, and from this aspect one refrains from doing the opposite of His will; and Solomon the king, peace be upon him, alluded to this, saying (Proverbs 27:18) "and he who watches over his master shall be honored" - and it is known that all "watching" is a negative commandment, as it is said (Eruvin 96a), "wherever it says 'watch,' 'lest,' or 'do not,' it is only a negative commandment" - and "he who watches over his master" is the attribute by which He, blessed be He, is called Adonai; and since this one is careful of his master's honor not to do the opposite of his will, it is fitting that he be honored in the World to Come, along the lines of "for those who honor Me I will honor" (I Samuel 2:30), which is explained in the Zohar, portion of Vayelech (285a): "for those who honor Me" in this world, "I will honor" in the World to Come.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:4: The second: to honor Him in order to perform His will and His commandments, and honor unqualified is in the aspect of a positive commandment, as our Sages, of blessed memory, say in Tractate Kiddushin, first chapter (31b): our Rabbis taught, what is "awe" and what is "honor"? "Awe" - he does not stand in his place, nor sit in his place, does not contradict his words, nor tip the scale against him. "Honor" - he feeds him and gives him drink, clothes him and covers him, brings him in and takes him out - so far. Along these lines it is explained in the Tikkunim (146b), "her honor is in the positive commandments," whose words we quoted in the Gate of Fear, chapter 5.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:5: What is found termed "honor" [kavod] in the books of the Prophets and Writings, most indicate the aspect of a positive commandment, along the lines of (Isaiah 24:14) "therefore in the lights [urim], honor the Lord," and likewise "for those who honor Me I will honor" - several aspects explained in the Zohar all indicate the aspect of a positive commandment. Likewise (ibid. 58:13) "and honor the holy day of the Lord" - our Sages, of blessed memory, explain (Shabbat 119a) that this refers to Yom Kippur, which has no eating or drinking - honor it with clean clothing. However, near this same verse, "honor" is found in the aspect of a negative commandment: "and honor it by not doing your own ways, from pursuing your own affairs, or speaking words [of business]."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:6: Likewise, besides this, "honor" is found in the aspect of fear, as in (Deuteronomy 28:58) "to fear this glorious and awesome Name" - it appears that His being awesome stems from His honor, which is called "glorious." So too the honor shown to the sages, to rise before them, stems from fear, as our Sages, of blessed memory, explain the verse (Ecclesiastes 8:13) "and it shall not be well with the wicked... because he does not fear before God" - concerning one who does not rise before his teacher - their words (Kiddushin 33b): Rabbi Elazar said, any Torah scholar who does not stand before his teacher is called wicked, does not live long, and his learning does not remain with him but is forgotten - "that it shall not be well with the wicked, and he shall not lengthen his days like a shadow, because he does not fear before God." This "awe," I would not know what it means, but when it says (Leviticus 19:32) "you shall rise up and you shall fear," this teaches that this "awe" refers to rising - so far. The plain sense of the verse is: he shall not lengthen his days, [being fleeting] like this shadow, which passes quickly, the reason being that it shall not be well with him, etc., because this wicked person does not fear before God to rise before his teacher - here explicitly, honor stemming from fear. So too they say in the midrash (Bemidbar Rabbah 7:2) that concerning the Levites, who did not sin with the Calf, "for those who honor Me I will honor" is said.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:7: Since we find honor stemming from fear, we saw fit to explain, at the end of this Gate, the conditions of the honor we are obligated to show our Maker, and thereby it will be recognized that we fear Him, in the two aspects mentioned regarding honor, which exist above. The aspect of honor in the matter of a positive commandment I already explained at the end of chapter 2 of this Gate, that Chochmah is called "kavod" because she serves through her thirty-two paths beneath the Crown [Keter], and likewise Tiferet serves and carries out the command of Father and Mother - here is the aspect of honor from the side of the positive.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:8: Further, honor is found from the side of fear, and this is the reason for the honor due to elders that we are commanded, as is said in the Idra of Naso (Zohar 131b) - his words: "and these are the thirteen adornments of the supernal beard, holy, most hidden of the hidden, mighty, to break and subdue all decrees of judgment; whoever sees the supernal, holy beard, most hidden of the hidden, is not put to shame by it, and therefore all its hairs are aged and mighty in their adornments" - so far. And in the Idra of Ha'azinu (289a), they term the supernal Elder by the name "kavod" [honor] - his words: "upon the beard of the Holy Ancient One depends all the preciousness of everything; it is called the mazal of everything, from that beard, mazal, the preciousness of all preciousness," etc. And at the end of his words: "therefore all preciousness of preciousness depends on this mazal" - so far. And since honor depends above, and there is the place of length of days, as is known, and one who does not accord honor to an elder or to his teacher, who occupies the place of an elder, and does not have fear to rise before him, will not lengthen his days - and it says "before God," and does not say "who does not fear God," to hint at the secret mentioned, along the lines of what Rashbi explains (Zohar, portion of Terumah 171a) concerning "before the Lord."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:9: According to the plain sense, it may also be understood, "before God" - meaning his teacher, who stands before the Shechinah, along the lines of "as the Lord lives, before whom I have stood" (see I Kings 17:1), and our Sages, of blessed memory, explain (Midrash Shmuel 8) that this means he stood before his teacher, Achiyah HaShiloni - here is an aspect of honor stemming from fear, even though it is in the aspect of the positive, as I explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:10: Therefore we saw fit to explain all the aspects of honor found in Torah, Prophets, and Writings pertaining to the practical honor of our Maker, and other things we are commanded to honor. The first thing we are obligated to do is to honor His great Name, and by honoring His Name we honor Him, since He and His Name are entirely one thing, and the honor of His Name is the Name YHVH and the other Names, for which the Name YHVH is the source; and one must show honor toward them - at least not to throw them about, and certainly not to erase them, for one who erases a holy Name transgresses a negative commandment. And it is not only concerning the honor of YHVH, but even ritual objects [tashmishei kedushah], one must show honor toward them, since once holiness and supernal illumination rested in those letters, holiness spreads through all those branches, and one must show honor toward them - this is the reason ritual objects require genizah [burial/storage].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:11: This is the reason for the honor due to the Torah scroll, since it is known that the Torah is His Name, as is explained in the Zohar several times (Va'etchanan 265b), and will be explained in its place, that just as His Name is called "glorious," as it says (Deuteronomy 28:58) "to fear the glorious Name," so too the Torah, which is His Name, must be honored - rising before it, and the Torah scroll should be clothed in a beautiful cloth, just as a person is obligated to clothe his father, etc. This is the matter found in several places in the Writings (Psalms 29:2) "give to the Lord the honor of His Name," and many like these.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:12: From this aspect, one must show honor toward all square script, even if not written with holiness, the reason being that since these letters are the likeness of the twenty-two holy forms by which all the worlds were created, and the lower letters indicate the intellectual forms cleaving to the Godhead, it is fitting to honor them, and if one finds them in the marketplace or other demeaning places, he should store them in a fitting place. Sefer Chasidim already says (siman 97) that a certain pious man was punished for not honoring found prayer-book pages and not sewing them together, see there. It seems to me that it is good to be careful, if one is reading and needs to stop for some reason, to close the book or cover it, out of honor for the Torah, lest, if left open, water or some filth fall on it, as this happens many times.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:13: The pious Rabbi Yosef Yaavetz, peace be upon him, writes in the Mishnah (Avot 4:6) "whoever honors the Torah, his own body is honored by people" - things pertaining to the matter of honor we are discussing; I have chosen to quote them here for their great practical benefit - his words: Rabbi Yehudah ibn Shoshan, of blessed memory, writes the reason: that one should recognize in his mind its greatness and the preciousness of its magnificent glory, for gold and glass cannot compare to it, and he should consider that it is called the strength of the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is said (Psalms 132:8) "You and the Ark of Your strength." And he should be exceedingly careful in the honor of the Torah itself, and in the honor of its sages, and in the honor of its books.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:14: Honor of the Torah itself, how? To engage in it always with a yearning soul, and to be exceedingly careful of its honor, that he be clean, and his hands and clothes clean, and the place have no filth in it - and I have a dispute with those who feign piety and read the zemirot [Sabbath hymns] in the marketplaces and streets without being careful whether there is filth there; and if they answer me, how can they leave their house for the synagogue without Torah [i.e., without a prayer book] - let him consider, and that is enough for him. Further, they should know and recognize that even for refraining from a transgression in the dark, they are given reward as though performing a mitzvah - and what mitzvah is greater and more exalted than that his whole body and limbs tremble before he mentions the Name, and he checks whether he is in a fitting place, and thereby fulfills the commandment "you shall fear the Lord your God" - and it is written (Malachi 2:5) "and he feared Me, and was afraid before My Name."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:15: And when he says, in the daily order [of prayers], "blessed is our God who created us for His glory and separated us from those who err," let him say it with settled mind and proper intent, like a person who saw a fiery furnace before him and was bound to be thrown into it, yet was saved and given dominion and greatness - and what fire consumes like the false religion of the idol-worshipers, and what dominion and greatness compares to the Torah of truth?
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:16: Likewise, he should do so when he blesses in public and listens to the prayer-leader reading the Torah, as it is said in the Zohar, that one who concentrates at that hour, his ears attentive and the eyes of his intellect open, is credited as though he received the Torah at Mount Sinai; and just as there was only a single voice there, so it should be fitting now.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:17: Honor of its sages, how? He should conduct himself toward them with great honor and awe, like the awe of Heaven, since their awe is included in "you shall fear the Lord your God," and he should fear them as though seeing the face of God - meaning, as though seeing the face of the King and his judges and officers.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:18: Honor of its books, how? He must beautify his books and place them and store them in the choicest place in his house, and cover them with a valued cloth; and just as people devise means and hang boards in the air to place food upon them, to protect them from mice and cats, so too he should do to protect the honor of Heaven. And when he moves them, he should not move them like other vessels, but rather in a manner of honor and modesty, like one who moves the king's garments in the king's presence, and should not touch them except with clean hands - these matters are entrusted to the heart, and one who fears God shall discharge them all.
